Water quality is determined by measuring biochemical properties of a
water body. Many organisms, including oysters and larval fish,
consistently require high-quality water to flourish. Human health, along
with Florida’s economy, also depends on the health of our waters.
Dissolved oxygen, dissolved oxygen saturation, salinity, water
temperature, and pH are crucial indicators of water quality. To ensure
that our waters meet standards established to protect aquatic life and
human well-being, each of these parameters are monitored by the state of
Florida as part of its responsibilities through the Clean Water Act
(Chapter 62-303, Florida Administrative Code).
